title: Snapshots, video and web embeds
summary: Capture a frame, render an animation video, or export a scene as an independent web component.

blocks.text: From an npm scene to an animation video

Create a [Studio project](/installation#create-with-studio), write your Scene, preview the choreography and render video using config.js. The generator includes the canvas host, local Studio and render defaults. [Manual npm setup](/installation#create-a-consumer-application) is available for existing applications.

The CLI serves the calling project’s index.html, launches a headless browser and sends captured frames to FFmpeg. The generated host starts src/scenes/Retiam.ts. A custom host can load other scene paths from the CLI’s file query parameter, as shown in the manual installation guide.

blocks.text: Offline stepping sets the frame interval from output FPS. That stabilizes timeline sampling but does not make network, browser media, wall-clock helpers or unseeded randomness deterministic. Preload assets and use scene-time updates for repeatable output.

Exact contracts: [Recorder](/api-recorder#recorder), [OfflineRecorder](/api-recorder#offlinerecorder), [OfflineRenderManager](/api-core#offlinerendermanager), [SnapshotManager](/api-core#snapshotmanager).
CLI preview and final render

Run the following from a generated project folder containing package.json and config.js. Retiam installs Puppeteer, Vite, ws and cli-progress as required production dependencies; RoughJS is included for retiam/rough. Chrome must support WebGPU, and FFmpeg must be available on PATH.

blocks.code:
cd my-animation
npm run check
npx retiam lint src/scenes/Retiam.ts --json
npx retiam render src/scenes/Retiam.ts

blocks.text: The render uses config.js without additional flags. With the generated defaults, the four-second starter produces a timestamped MP4 under outputs/video. For a smaller draft, override the dimensions and frame rate:

blocks.code:
npx retiam render src/scenes/Retiam.ts -w 1280 -h 720 -f 30 -d 4000
npx retiam snapshot src/scenes/Retiam.ts --times 1.0,2.2,3.0 --json

blocks.text: In a manually created project, replace src/scenes/Retiam.ts with the scene path used by its host, such as scenes/MyScene.ts. Use npm install retiam@latest to install the current engine in an existing npm project.

Render duration is milliseconds; snapshot --times is seconds. --out selects a directory. Snapshot writes PNG files; its wall-clock timing gives approximate preview checks. Render filenames include a timestamp.

maxDuration: 0 renders until the scene finishes. Set a positive millisecond limit for scenes with loops or ongoing updates, and keep a final hold when the last state needs reading time. Inspect the exported video for its first frame, transitions, final state and audio.
Render configuration

Every generated project contains config.js with output and renderer quality settings. The render command forwards every supported engine field to the scene renderer. A manual project can copy the same file.

The renderer begins with built-in defaults, loads the selected config file from the current project folder, then applies command-line overrides. If retiam.config.js exists, it takes priority over config.js. Only the selected file is loaded.

cells: Output directory, resolved from the project root.

Supersampling scale and WebGPU MSAA sample count.
Raytracing is off by default; denoising is used when it is enabled.

blocks.text: The remaining settings control transparency layers, shadows and culling, ray samples and bounces, accumulation, gamma, BVH construction and the OIDN model. The comments in the complete file list the selectable enum values. Surface appearance is authored in the scene through scene.shading and material.shading; see [3D materials](/three-d#material-properties). Exact contracts: [RenderConfig](/api-render#renderconfig).

This command overrides fps, maxDuration and outputDir while keeping the other file settings. Partial config files also work: omitted fields use built-in defaults. These are CLI render settings; Studio’s interactive preview is controlled through its own UI and scene code.

blocks.content: Puppeteer is a required production dependency of Retiam. Video rendering also requires Chrome with WebGPU and FFmpeg. Native denoising additionally requires oidnDenoise; select raytraceEnabled: true and denoiser: "native", or pass --raytrace --raw.

blocks.text: Standalone embeds

An independent embed contains the scene and the engine code it needs. For a generated project or another external npm application, follow [the package-based recipe](/export#embed-from-npm) below. The CLI shown in this section is the repository-layout exporter, which emits a retiam-scene component.

Export writes a lowercase scene-name IIFE bundle and registers the retiam/retiam-scene custom elements. Copy the output directory with any emitted assets to the receiving site. The bundle can run independently of a separate Retiam installation; remote asset URLs or speech services used by the scene still need to be packaged locally or supplied at runtime.

blocks.title: Current exporter setup
blocks.content: The exporter in this checkout generates src/_temp_embed_entry.ts with an import of ./engine/_core/Scene and source-tree aliases. That command currently expects the engine repository layout. External npm projects need a package-based export entry before using this CLI path; the independent runtime of the completed bundle is the intended output. This setup constraint is separate from using Retiam as an npm library for authoring and video rendering.

blocks.text: Build an independent embed from an npm project

Bundle a scene directly from an external npm project using its installed package and Vite. Add the component entry below as src/embed.ts. The example imports scenes/MyScene.ts from manual setup; in a generated project, change the import to MyScene from "./scenes/Retiam". This recipe uses Vite 6, matching create-retiam; use the same version in a manually configured application.

blocks.code:
// Generated project: first line of src/embed.ts
import MyScene from "./scenes/Retiam";

blocks.text: Each element owns its canvas and scene. Disconnecting it removes the resize observer and destroys the scene; a pending startup cleans up when it settles. The observer bridges element-size changes to the composer’s current window-resize mechanism. scene-ready means startup has completed, not that the animation has reached its final frame. Errors during initialization appear inside the element; Scene.run reports later choreography failures through the engine.

Save the following as vite.embed.config.ts. Its ES module output includes the imported engine code, with any chunks/assets emitted by the bundler. Do not mark retiam external: doing that would require a separate runtime import.
Copy the whole outputs/embed directory into the receiving site, for example at /embeds/my-scene/. Load the emitted module and give its element a nonzero display size:

The receiving page needs WebGPU and the exported files, but does not need npm, an engine CDN or the authoring project. Serve the files over HTTP from a supported secure origin, preserving relative asset paths. Network URLs explicitly used by the scene remain dependencies; localize those assets and avoid service-backed features when a fully offline bundle is required.

Give a different scene bundle its own custom-element name. A browser registers a name once; loading two different bundles that both register my-retiam-scene does not create two selectable scene definitions. Test two instances, an element resize, and removal during startup before integrating the component into a client-side router.

For a CMS or blog that accepts custom HTML, host the build output on an HTTPS origin and paste the module script and custom element shown above. In React or another client-rendered application, load the module once and mount the same custom element; unmounting triggers its cleanup. Keep element dimensions explicit.

For a browser page that already hosts your authored code and can depend on jsDelivr, [the CDN method](/installation#use-the-cdn) avoids making a separate component bundle. Use the embed build when you want to deploy the finished scene and its emitted engine files together.
Audio, replay and native denoising

Input replay uses --replay with the recorded JSON. Audio is mixed and muxed through the supported timeline/capture path. Native denoising uses --raytrace --raw and requires oidnDenoise plus FFmpeg. Inspect the exported result for media alignment, subtitle placement, frame pacing and noise before publishing it.
